headline: Google takes a -5% hammering last night as top AI researchers bolt to rivals — and Labor's CGT/negative gearing deal is done, with major implications for property investors.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: GOOG got smacked last night — down 5% — after multiple top AI researchers from DeepMind and the Gemini team defected to OpenAI and Anthropic. Markets hate talent drain at the best of times, but losing your AI scientists when the whole company's value is tied to AI leadership? That's a proper hit to confidence. The stock had been sitting around $367 before this news broke.

movers.name: Global X Artificial Intelligence ETF
movers.note: GXAI fell 3.2% today, dragged down by the same Google/Alphabet story — the ETF has meaningful exposure to Alphabet and other big-name AI companies that slid last night on the NASDAQ. When the AI sector's headline stock drops 5%, the AI-focused ETF follows it down.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft dropped 3.2% last night in a broader NASDAQ tech sell-off. The NASDAQ fell 1.3% overall, with big-cap tech taking the brunt. MSFT is now down roughly 20% from its highs this year, and analysts are starting to debate whether the valuation is getting attractive — but there's no fresh positive catalyst yet.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: PLS slipped another 1.1% today, continuing its tough run — now sitting 18.8% below what you paid. There's no single news shock today; it's more a reflection of subdued lithium prices. The more interesting story is that analysts at Fastmarkets are flagging that lithium demand is starting to outpace supply — a potential longer-term tailwind, but the market isn't pricing it in yet.

movers.name: Vanguard FTSE Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE dipped 0.87% today. The Aussie dollar fell about 0.7% against the USD, which works against this ETF's unhedged emerging market holdings when converted back to AUD. No major emerging market-specific news today.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG eased 0.5% today, reflecting the mild softness across global equity markets. As a diversified fund holding Australian and international shares, it tends to absorb these daily moves without too much drama. You're still just ahead of your cost base overall.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market Shares ETF
movers.note: VTS dipped 0.47% today on the ASX, reflecting last night's S&P 500 softness (down 0.37%) and the weaker AUD/USD. The US total market was broadly softer, with tech leading losses on the NASDAQ. Still sitting just above your cost base.

movers.name: BetaShares Global Energy Companies ETF
movers.note: FUEL was flat today, up just a fraction. That's actually a decent result given crude oil (WTI) fell nearly 3% last night to $72.67/barrel. The ASX-listed ETF often lags moves in the underlying oil price by a session, so watch for possible softness tomorrow if oil stays down.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: TTWO was essentially flat last night, nudging up 0.12%. The stock has been buoyed by excitement around GTA VI pre-sale announcements driving a recent surge, and it's holding those gains. No new news overnight — the market is just sitting and waiting on the GTA VI launch catalyst.

watch_today.title: GOOG: Talent exodus is a real risk — hold for now
watch_today.detail: Google lost multiple senior AI researchers from DeepMind and the Gemini team to OpenAI and Anthropic in the past 48 hours — including a Nobel laureate. The stock dropped 5% last night to $348.78. You're still 13.5% up overall on your small position, but this is a genuine concern, not just noise. The competitive moat Google has in AI depends heavily on who's building it. Hold — don't panic sell, but watch closely for any further departures or management response.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX: AI ETF down 3.2% — hold and watch
watch_today.detail: Your AI ETF fell 3.2% today, tracking the Google-led AI sector sell-off. At $17.79, you're now $17.25 in the red on this position (-5.8%). The Google talent story is the key risk here — if it escalates, this ETF will feel it again. But if it's a one-off wobble and Google responds, there's recovery potential. Hold for now, but this is one to watch closely this week.

watch_today.title: FUEL.AX: Oil down nearly 3% last night — possible softness tomorrow
watch_today.detail: Crude oil fell $2.15 to $72.67/barrel last night — a 2.87% drop. FUEL.AX only moved fractionally today because ASX energy ETFs often lag the oil price move by a session. If oil stays weak tonight, expect FUEL to feel it at tomorrow's open. Worth keeping an eye on, but no action needed unless oil drops further.

watch_today.title: Labor + Greens CGT & negative gearing deal — done
watch_today.detail: Labor has reached a deal with the Greens to pass capital gains tax (CGT) reforms and changes to negative gearing. CGT is the tax you pay when you sell an investment at a profit — the current 50% discount (meaning you only pay tax on half your gain) is reportedly being wound back. Negative gearing, where property investors claim losses against their income, is also being tightened on existing properties. This is significant for any property investors in your network — and could affect broader investor sentiment in the market this week.

watch_today.title: TTWO: GTA VI excitement holding — keep holding
watch_today.detail: Take-Two was flat last night at $239.57, consolidating after recent gains fuelled by GTA VI pre-sale announcements. You're up 4.5% on this position. The real catalyst — the actual game launch — is still ahead. Nothing to do here except sit tight and let the story play out.

watch_today.title: RBA rate outlook: Aussie dollar slipping
watch_today.detail: The AUD fell to 0.6957 USD today (down 0.66%), even as some traders are still pricing in a possible RBA rate rise. Major banks are reportedly split on the outlook — some saying the RBA's recent warning will act 'like a hammer' on borrowing, others less convinced. A weaker AUD is a mild tailwind for your unhedged US holdings (GOOG, MSFT, TTWO) when converted back to AUD.

politics.summary: Two big stories dominating Australian politics today: Labor and the Greens have sealed a deal on capital gains tax and negative gearing reforms, and the RBA interest rate outlook is dividing the major banks. Both have direct implications for investors and property owners.

stories.title: Labor and Greens seal deal on CGT and negative gearing reforms
stories.why_it_matters: Labor has locked in the Greens' support to pass changes to capital gains tax (CGT) and negative gearing — two of the biggest tax perks for Australian investors and property owners. The CGT discount (currently 50%, meaning you only pay tax on half a profit when you sell an investment) is set to be wound back, and negative gearing on existing investment properties will be tightened. A news.com.au report also confirms the end date has been set on what's described as a '$33 billion tax perk.' This will hit property investors hardest, but it also affects anyone selling shares or other assets at a profit. Expect significant debate this week as the legislation moves through parliament.

stories.title: Major banks split on RBA rate outlook after interest rate warning
stories.why_it_matters: Australia's major banks are publicly disagreeing on what the RBA (Reserve Bank of Australia) will do with interest rates next. The RBA recently issued what realestate.com.au describes as a rate 'warning,' and one bank is saying it will hit borrowers 'like a hammer.' Others are less alarmed. For mortgage holders and property investors, the direction of rates matters enormously — a rate rise would push up repayments. The Aussie dollar is also being kept afloat by traders who think the RBA might still lift rates, per AFR reporting today.

stories.title: Labor's tax overhaul also includes NDIS delays and new superannuation restrictions
stories.why_it_matters: The Labor-Greens tax deal is broader than just CGT and negative gearing. The SMH reports the package also includes delays to some NDIS (National Disability Insurance Scheme) spending, and Yahoo Finance Australia flags new restrictions on superannuation (the exact details of the 'ban' for millions of Australians are still emerging). This is a significant legislative package — the full detail will matter a lot for how it affects different groups of Australians.

ai.summary: The AI world is fixated on one story today: Google is hemorrhaging top talent. Multiple senior researchers from DeepMind and the Gemini team have left for OpenAI and Anthropic in just 48 hours — and the market has punished the stock for it. There's also a positive side story: Google DeepMind has partnered with acclaimed film studio A24 on a first-of-its-kind research collaboration.

stories.title: Google loses multiple top DeepMind and Gemini AI researchers to OpenAI and Anthropic
stories.source: Search Engine Journal / Investor's Business Daily
stories.why_it_matters: In a 48-hour span, Google has lost at least two senior AI researchers — one reportedly a Nobel laureate — who have joined rival firms OpenAI and Anthropic. The departures are from Google's most prestigious AI teams: DeepMind (responsible for breakthroughs like AlphaFold) and the Gemini team (Google's flagship AI model). Multiple reports are asking whether internal confidence at Google is collapsing. Alphabet's share price dropped 5% last night to $348.78 directly in response. For GOOG and GXAI.AX holders, this is the key story of the week — Google's entire market premium rests on its AI leadership.

stories.title: Google DeepMind partners with film studio A24 on AI research collaboration
stories.why_it_matters: Amid the talent exodus gloom, Google DeepMind announced a first-of-its-kind research partnership with A24, the indie film studio behind films like 'Everything Everywhere All at Once' and 'Midsommar.' The partnership will explore how AI can be applied to creative storytelling and filmmaking — a signal that Google is pushing DeepMind into applied creative industries, not just pure research. It's a small positive amid a tough news day for Alphabet, but shows the company is still actively building commercial applications for its AI work.

stories.title: South Australia pushes for AI data centres; industry says it's not seeking subsidies
stories.why_it_matters: South Australia is actively lobbying to attract AI data centres — the massive computing facilities that power AI models — as part of a broader economic push. The AI industry, for its part, says it's not looking for government handouts (subsidies), just supportive conditions like reliable energy and planning approvals. For Australian investors, this signals that AI infrastructure build-out is becoming a local story, not just a US one — and could benefit Australian energy and infrastructure plays down the line.

stories.title: Alphabet shares also under pressure from AI capex concerns
stories.why_it_matters: Beyond the talent story, there's a secondary pressure on Alphabet: the company's huge spending on AI infrastructure (capex — capital expenditure, meaning money spent on building data centres and computing hardware) is weighing on investor sentiment. The stock had been trading around $367 after strong Q1 earnings, but the combination of heavy spending commitments and now the talent departures has pushed it down to $348. Google's CEO has said AI has 'completely changed the revenue picture' — but investors want to see that spending translate into profit faster.

sport.summary: NRL Round 17 is locked and loaded this week, with the Titans hosting the Bulldogs at Cbus Super Stadium on Friday — your Gold Coast local game. The big injury story today is Latrell Mitchell, whose injury is reportedly worse than first feared. There's also Wimbledon news and some AFL transfer drama.

stories.title: Latrell Mitchell injury worse than first feared — mammoth blow for his club
stories.why_it_matters: Latrell Mitchell's injury has been upgraded to more serious than initially thought, Fox Sports reports — described as a 'mammoth blow' for his club's premiership ambitions. The article doesn't specify the exact injury or timeline, but the language suggests he could miss significant time. His club had been considered a finals contender, so his absence reshapes the back half of the season considerably. Worth checking Fox Sports for the full breakdown on timeframe.

stories.title: NRL Round 17 team lists confirmed — Titans vs Bulldogs your local game Friday
stories.why_it_matters: Round 17 team lists are out. Your local game is Titans vs Bulldogs at Cbus Super Stadium on Friday at 6:00pm — worth getting across the team news before kick-off. The NRL judiciary also handed down fines to Jason Taumalolo, Angus Verrills, Dallin Watene-Zelezniak (Marzhew) and Jake Smithies following Round 16 incidents. Broncos fans will be pleased to hear Ben Hunt has re-signed to stay in Brisbane.

stories.title: Serena Williams earns Wimbledon singles wildcard — comeback continues
stories.why_it_matters: Serena Williams has been awarded a wildcard into the Wimbledon singles draw, continuing her much-publicised return to professional tennis. Wimbledon begins in early July, and Serena's presence will make it must-watch TV regardless of where she's seeded. At 44, it's an extraordinary sporting story — expect wall-to-wall coverage as the tournament approaches.

stories.title: AFL: Isaac Butters drops cryptic free agency hint; Demons caught up in May case fallout
stories.why_it_matters: Two big AFL stories today: Power midfielder Isaac Butters has given a cryptic one-word answer ('interesting') when asked about his free agency plans, sending the AFL world into a spin about which club he might choose. Meanwhile, Melbourne Demons are dealing with the fallout from the Steven May saga — reports suggest it could derail the club's season, with Nine describing it as potentially the 'biggest fallout' of the year. The Demons were considered a top-four contender, so the instability around May is a serious issue for their finals push.
